title: Digital Gatekeepers: Exploring Large Language Model’s Role in Immigration Decisions
findings: Both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, similar to human evaluators, showed a significant preference for admitting immigrant applicants who were escaping political/religious persecution. This preference was stronger than for applicants seeking to reunite with family. For instance, GPT-4 was 15.6% more likely to accept an applicant escaping persecution. The models also demonstrated an interaction effect, preferring applicants escaping persecution who had not previously visited the U.S., as prior visits might cast doubt on the sincerity of their asylum claim.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the preference of Large Language Models in hypothetical immigration admission scenarios, specifically evaluating how the reason 'Escape political/religious persecution' influenced the decision to admit an applicant compared to other reasons like 'Seek better job' or 'Reunite with family'.
